item.title: Mint: Distributed Compute-Optimal LLM Training Framework
item.description:
View on GitHub · Architecture · Quickstart · Key Innovations

Mint is a high-performance, compute-optimal distributed training, fine-tuning, and alignment framework engineered for Large Language Models. Designed to achieve maximum parameter throughput at lowest hardware cost, Mint runs seamlessly across both Apple Silicon (MPS / Metal) and high-density NVIDIA CUDA GPU clusters.

Architecture & Modules 

flowchart TD
Config["Compute Budget FLOPs / Hardware Specs"] --> Planner["Compute-Optimal Auto-Planner"]
Planner -->|"Chinchilla Scaled Hyperparameters"| Engine["Mint Training Engine"]
subgraph DataEngine["Distributed Streaming Data Engine"]
StreamDataloader["Streaming Chunk Dataloader"]
Mixer["Multi-Dataset Blending (SmolTalk / GSM8K / ClimbMix)"]
StreamDataloader --> Mixer
end
subgraph CoreEngine["Optimization & Parallelism"]
ZeRO["ZeRO-2 Optimizer State Sharding"]
Muon["Distributed MuonAdamW + norMuon Polar Express"]
Kernels["Hardware Kernels (Apple Metal MPS & FlashAttention-2)"]
KVCache["Optimized Paged KV-Cache & SwiGLU / RoPE"]
end
Engine --> StreamDataloader
Mixer --> ZeRO
ZeRO --> Muon
Muon --> Kernels
Kernels --> KVCache
KVCache --> Pretrain["Pre-Training (Gemma / TikToken)"]
KVCache --> SFT["Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT v1 / v2)"]
KVCache --> DPO["Direct Preference Optimization (DPO v1 / v2)"]

Module Breakdown

Package Module Purpose
mint.nn Transformer architectures, RoPE (Rotary Position Embeddings), RMSNorm, SwiGLU MLP layers
mint.optim Distributed MuonAdamW optimizer with norMuon normalization and Polar Express coefficients, alongside ZeRO-2 sharding
mint.data Zero-memory-bloat streaming chunk dataloaders for pre-training and preference datasets
mint.trainer Distributed multi-GPU / multi-device training orchestrator supporting PyTorch DDP and Apple Metal (MPS)
mint.sft Supervised fine-tuning pipeline for custom models and HuggingFace backbones (e.g. Qwen2, Llama)
mint.eval Distributed evaluation suite covering conversational benchmarks, GSM8K reasoning, and MCQ tasks
mint.kvcache Low-overhead Key-Value cache implementation for high-throughput inference and validation

What Makes Mint Special?

1. Automated Compute Optimality

Mint automatically calculates scaling-law optimal parameters (dataset token count, layer depth, hidden dimension, and learning rate schedules) based on the user’s available FLOP budget and cluster memory constraints.

2. Distributed MuonAdamW Optimizer

Integrates the state-of-the-art Muon matrix optimizer alongside AdamW, utilizing norMuon normalization with Polar Express coefficients for faster convergence and lower loss variance on modern transformer architectures.

3. ZeRO-2 Sharding & Distributed Dataloaders

  • ZeRO-2 Sharding: Partitions optimizer states and gradients across available ranks to enable training larger models on memory-constrained GPUs.
  • Custom Streaming Dataloaders: Streams pre-tokenized shards directly from disk or cloud buckets without memory bloat.

4. Cross-Platform Acceleration

  • Apple Silicon (MPS): Native Metal Performance Shaders integration for local M-series Mac training and fine-tuning.
  • NVIDIA CUDA: Supports PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), FlashAttention-2, and bfloat16 mixed precision.

Quickstart & CLI Commands

Installation 

# Clone and install Mint
git clone https://github.com/nagarajpoojari404/mint.git
cd mint
uv pip install -e .

Pre-Training 

# Pre-train a custom transformer model
uv run mint pretrain --config configs/config_d12_pretrain.toml

# Stream training across sharded datasets
uv run mint stream-train \
 --num-train-shards 4 \
 --min-shards 1 \
 --train-script scripts/pretrain.py \
 --train-args "--config configs/config_d12_pretrain.toml"

Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) 

# SFT on custom architectures
uv run mint sft --config configs/config_d12_sft.toml

# SFT on HuggingFace models (e.g. Qwen2, Llama) with curated datasets
uv run mint v2-sft \
 --config configs/config_hf_sft.toml \
 --model-name Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B \
 --datasets gsm8k smoltalk

Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) 

# DPO alignment against a reference model
uv run mint dpo \
 --config configs/config_d12_dpo.toml \
 --ref-model checkpoints/checkpoint_step_10.pt

# HuggingFace DPO
uv run mint v2-dpo \
 --model-name Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B \
 --config configs/config_hf_dpo.toml

Dataset Utilities Included

  • mint prepare-dpo: Prepares preference pairs (chosen vs. rejected responses).
  • mint download-climbmix: Downloads and tokenizes curated reasoning and code pre-training datasets.
  • mint --help: Lists all CLI commands and configuration options.

item.title: Quantum Threads: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Deep Learning
item.description:
View on GitHub · Architecture · Key Innovations

Quantum Threads is an applied quantum machine learning research and engineering project that benchmarks hybrid quantum-classical neural network architectures for fine-grained underwater animal classification across 23 marine species (>13,000 images in the UAD-2023 dataset).

The project develops hybrid counterparts to premier classical computer vision models—Hybrid Quantum ResNet-18, Hybrid Quantum ResNet-50, and Hybrid Quantum Inception-V3—incorporating Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQCs) as high-dimensional non-linear quantum kernels.

Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pipeline 

flowchart LR
Input["Underwater Image (224x224x3)"] --> ClassicalCNN["Pre-trained Backbone (ResNet-50 / InceptionV3)"]
ClassicalCNN --> FeatureVec["Latent Feature Vector (512-d)"]
FeatureVec --> AngleEncoding["Quantum Angle Encoding"]
subgraph QPU["Cloud QPU (IBM Quantum)"]
AngleEncoding --> PQC["Parameterized Quantum Circuit"]
PQC --> Entanglement["CNOT Entangling & Rotation Gates"]
Entanglement --> Measurement["Pauli-Z Expectation Measurement"]
end
Measurement --> ClassicalHead["Classification Head (23 Classes)"]
ClassicalHead --> Loss["Cross-Entropy Loss"]
Loss -->|"Adjoint Differentiation"| Optimizer["Adam Optimizer"]
Optimizer -->|"Update Circuit Angles"| PQC

What Makes It Innovative?

1. Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQC) as Quantum Kernels

By embedding classical feature embeddings into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces using rotational gates (Rx,Ry,RzR_x, R_y, R_zRx​,Ry​,Rz​) and multi-qubit CNOT entangling layers, the quantum circuit maps non-linearly separable marine feature vectors into linearly separable quantum states.

2. Adjoint Differentiation

Rather than relying on parameter-shift rules that require 2N2N2N quantum circuit executions per step (where NNN is parameter count), the system leverages reversible state-vector adjoint differentiation to compute analytical quantum gradients with constant memory and execution overhead.

3. Distributed Cloud QPU Orchestration

Distributes parallel quantum kernel evaluation batches across multiple IBM Quantum Cloud QPUs and state-vector simulators, mitigating queue latency during large-scale model training.

Research Results & Comparison

Model Architecture Quantum Kernel Type Top-1 Accuracy Parameter Count Training Convergence
ResNet-18 (Classical) Standard Dense 87.4% 11.2M 45 epochs
Hybrid Quantum ResNet-18 8-Qubit Entangled PQC 89.8% 11.1M 32 epochs
ResNet-50 (Classical) Standard Dense 91.2% 23.5M 50 epochs
Hybrid Quantum ResNet-50 16-Qubit Multi-Layer PQC 93.6% 23.4M 38 epochs
Hybrid Inception-V3 16-Qubit PQC 92.9% 21.8M 36 epochs

Running on Real IBM Quantum Hardware 

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/nagarajpoojari404/Quantum-Threads.git
cd Quantum-Threads

# Install dependencies (Qiskit, PennyLane, PyTorch)
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure IBM Quantum API credentials in config.toml
export IBM_QUANTUM_TOKEN="your_ibm_quantum_api_token"

# Train hybrid model
python train_hybrid.py --backbone resnet50 --qubits 8 --shots 1024

item.title: Video Interpolation AI: Vision Transformers for Frame Synthesis
item.description:
View on GitHub · Model Architecture · Empirical Results

Video Interpolation AI is an applied deep learning project implementing state-of-the-art Video Frame Interpolation Transformers (VIFT) and comparing their performance against classical and CNN-based approaches such as Deep Voxel Flow (DVF) and Super SloMo.

The goal is to synthesize temporally coherent intermediate frames between consecutive video inputs (I0,I1→I0.5I_0, I_1 \to I_{0.5}I0​,I1​→I0.5​), transforming low-framerate footage (e.g. 15 or 24 FPS) into buttery-smooth 60+ FPS video without motion blur or warping artifacts.

Architectural Comparison 

flowchart TD
FramePair["Input Frame Pair (Frame t, Frame t+1)"] --> ModelSelect{"Model Architecture"}
ModelSelect -->|"Traditional Optical Flow"| DVF["Deep Voxel Flow (DVF)"]
ModelSelect -->|"U-Net Flow Estimation"| SloMo["Super SloMo"]
ModelSelect -->|"Swin Attention SOTA"| VIFT["VIFT (Transformer)"]
DVF --> SynthDVF["Synthesized Frame (Blur & Occlusion Errors)"]
SloMo --> SynthSloMo["Synthesized Frame (Quadratic Compute Cost)"]
VIFT --> SynthVIFT["Synthesized Frame (High PSNR & Linear Compute)"]

Why Transformers for Video Interpolation?

  1. Deep Voxel Flow (DVF):

    • Relies strictly on optical flow vectors and bilinear warping.
    • Fails on non-rigid motion, rapid object acceleration, and specular reflections.

  2. Super SloMo:

    • Replaces traditional optical flow with bi-directional flow estimation and U-Net refinement.
    • Requires substantial computational resources (>39M>39\text{M}>39M parameters) and experiences quadratic scaling issues with resolution.

  3. Video Frame Interpolation Transformer (VIFT):

    • Leverages Swin Transformer (Shifted Window) attention blocks to compute self-attention within local windows while cross-attending across window boundaries.
    • Reduces computational complexity from quadratic O(N2)O(N^2)O(N2) to linear O(N)O(N)O(N) with respect to image resolution.
    • Captures both micro-textures and long-range motion trajectories accurately.

Benchmark Results

Evaluated across standard Vimeo-90K and UCF101 interpolation benchmark datasets:

Model Architecture Parameter Count (M) PSNR (dB) ↑\uparrow↑ SSIM ↑\uparrow↑ Inference Speed (FPS)
Deep Voxel Flow (DVF) 12.8 M 29.42 0.892 42
Super SloMo 39.6 M 33.15 0.941 18
VIFT (Ours / Transformer) 14.2 M 35.84 0.968 38

PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure) demonstrate superior frame reconstruction quality.

Quickstart & Inference 

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/nagarajpoojari404/video-interpolation-AI.git
cd video-interpolation-AI

# Install dependencies (PyTorch, Torchvision, OpenCV)
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run video interpolation pipeline (2x or 4x FPS upscaling)
python interpolate.py \
 --input ./data/sample_low_fps.mp4 \
 --output ./output_60fps.mp4 \
 --scale 2 \
 --checkpoint ./weights/vift_best.pth

item.title: Gluon AI: Intelligent VS Code Documentation Assistant
item.description:
View on GitHub · Features · Architecture

Gluon AI is a developer productivity extension for Visual Studio Code designed to eliminate the friction of writing code documentation and reverse-engineering unfamiliar codebases. Powered by GPT models, Gluon AI analyzes selected code snippets, function definitions, or entire modules to generate accurate, formatted docstrings, type annotations, and technical summaries directly inside the IDE.

How It Works 

flowchart LR
Editor["Developer Selects Code in Editor"] --> Command["Trigger Gluon AI Command"]
Command --> Parser["AST & Context Extractor"]
Parser --> PromptGen["Prompt Generator"]
PromptGen --> LLM["LLM API Endpoint"]
LLM --> Streamer["Response Streaming Handler"]
Streamer --> InlineDoc["Insert Formatted Docstrings"]

Key Capabilities

  1. One-Click Docstring Generation:

    • Inspects function signatures, parameter types, return values, and thrown exceptions.
    • Generates standard docstring formats tailored to the active language (JSDoc, Google/NumPy Docstrings in Python, GoDoc, RustDoc).

  2. Context-Aware Code Explanation:

    • Explains complex algorithms, regular expressions, and convoluted legacy logic in clean, human-readable language.

  3. Refactoring Suggestions & Complexity Analysis:

    • Identifies time/space complexity bottlenecks, edge-case vulnerabilities, and opportunities for cleaner functional abstractions.

  4. Multi-Language Support:

    • First-class support for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, C/C++, Rust, and Java.

Installation & Setup

From Source 

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/nagarajpoojari404/Gluon-AI.git
cd Gluon-AI

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Compile TypeScript
npm run compile

# Press F5 in VS Code to launch the Extension Development Host

Configuration

Set your OpenAI API key in VS Code Settings:

{
 "gluonAI.apiKey": "sk-...",
 "gluonAI.model": "gpt-3.5-turbo",
 "gluonAI.docstringStyle": "auto"
}

Usage Shortcuts

  • Explain Code: Select code →\to→ Ctrl + Shift + P →\to→ Gluon AI: Explain Selected Code
  • Generate Docstrings: Place cursor above function →\to→ Ctrl + Shift + P →\to→ Gluon AI: Generate Docstring
